design_findings: Windows exclusive locking must avoid the bounded nonce-read region; locks reserve [4096,4097), without extending the file.
A dedicated manual-reset event avoids unrelated overlapped requests signalling a shared file handle. All pending paths drain before request storage is released.
Removed an in-development callback test seam that could unwind while a stack OVERLAPPED remained pending. Final production lock dispatch has no such callbacks.

Nonce creation and synchronization precede ownership acquisition under shared admission; no actionable record can refer to that owner before acquisition returns. Interrupted initialization preserves a bounded orphan.
limitations: Coordinator, descriptor-relative storage, private validation and operation-lock randomness remain Unix-only. The Windows file-lock backend alone is not a Windows recovery adapter.
No production mutation acquires recovery admission yet. Whole-intent worker propagation, durable replacement, live inspection/reconciliation and recovery UI integration remain required.

Blocking waiter tests check non-completion while held and completion after release; scheduling can delay a thread before its syscall, so they do not deterministically prove a particular pending OS interleaving.
Process termination tests run on Linux and verify OS lock release plus unchanged readable evidence; they do not establish sudden-power-loss durability.
No Windows/macOS runtime, native UI screenshot, startup measurement, measured speedup or full release acceptance this checkpoint.

Unlock failure is logged during guard Drop; closing the owned File provides the final OS release. Pending Windows completion has no timeout and can wait on a stalled filesystem. Recovery work must stay on blocking owners.
